review_notes: I read the whole file. I searched Mathlib for other definitions of depth or grade, including the pattern `sSup {n : ℕ∞ | ∀ i ...}`. The only other hits were `WType.depth` (the depth of a W-type tree) and `Order.grade` (a graded-order function). Neither is related to module depth. The file defines `ModuleCat.depth`, `Ideal.depth` and `IsLocalRing.depth`, which are layered specialisations of one definition and not competing versions. The regular-sequence characterisations use the existing `RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular`, and the Ext vanishing uses the existing `Ext`. The ulift and iso invariance lemmas are theorem-level statements and are outside this rubric. I found no avoidable duplicate concept. I did not check other parts of the library for a concept under a different name, such as a general "Ext-vanishing index", but I saw no sign of one.
